Dan Ahlers

Democratic candidate for Governor and Lieutenant Governor, South Dakota · Challenger

Small business owner; executive director of the South Dakota Democratic Party (on leave from his duties during the campaign)

Dan Ahlers is a small business owner from Dell Rapids who served six years in the South Dakota Legislature, in both the House and the Senate. He was the 2020 Democratic nominee for U.S. Senate and has been executive director of the South Dakota Democratic Party since 2023. He announced his campaign for governor in February 2026 and is the Democratic nominee in the November 3, 2026 general election against Republican Gov. Larry Rhoden.

Where Ahlers stands

Health care
Says the state's top priority should be its health care crisis, including nursing home closures, rural hospitals losing services and keeping doctors and other medical professionals in the state.
Taxes
Says South Dakota does not need a state income tax and points to the state's ongoing budget surpluses.
Cost of living
Names cost of living, including property taxes, utility costs and inflation, as one of his top concerns, along with fair taxes.
Data centers
Says local governments should have more authority over where data centers are built and how they use local resources.
Economic development
Proposes shifting economic development money toward small businesses. He questions the return on a $69 million state incentive given to a single Sioux Falls company.
Education
Calls education "incredibly important" and says families should not be charged for school lunches at all.
Tribal relations
Proposes restoring a tribal relations commission with representatives from all nine South Dakota tribes. He would give tribal governments a stronger role in decisions on public safety, education, health care and economic development.

Background

  • Born November 14, 1973, in Dell Rapids, South Dakota
  • Degree in government and international relations, Augustana University
  • Opened a video rental store in Dell Rapids in 1999, later with stores in Hartford and Tea; opened The Jabberwock coffee shop in 2008
  • Former president of the Dell Rapids Chamber of Commerce (12 years, until 2021)
  • Served six years in the South Dakota Legislature, in the House and the Senate (District 25)
  • 2020 Democratic nominee for U.S. Senate (lost to Mike Rounds)
  • Executive director of the South Dakota Democratic Party since 2023
  • 2026 Democratic nominee for governor; running mate Steven McCleerey
